questions.stem: The NATIONAL ANIMAL of India is:
questions.explanation: National animal: Royal Bengal Tiger (since 1973, adopted when Project Tiger was launched). Before 1973, the lion was India's national animal. National aquatic animal: Ganges river dolphin. National heritage animal: Elephant.

questions.stem: The NATIONAL BIRD of India is:
questions.explanation: Indian Peafowl (Pavo cristatus) — declared national bird on 26 January 1963. Protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972. Found widely across India; associated with Lord Krishna iconography.

questions.explanation: Platanista gangetica — declared national aquatic animal in October 2009. Nearly blind; uses echolocation. Classified as Endangered by IUCN. Found in the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and their tributaries. Largest population in Bihar's Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary.

questions.explanation: Lotus — sacred flower in Hindu and Buddhist traditions; symbol of purity. National tree: Banyan (Ficus benghalensis). National fruit: Mango. National river: Ganges (declared 2008).

questions.stem: The ONE-HORNED RHINOCEROS is majorly protected in which national park?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga (Assam) — home to two-thirds of the world's Indian one-horned rhinoceros population (~2,600+ of global ~3,700). UNESCO WHS 1985. Also has tigers, elephants, wild buffalo. Jim Corbett — tiger reserve. Ranthambore — tiger reserve (Rajasthan).

questions.stem: Project TIGER was launched in India in the year:
questions.explanation: Project Tiger launched 1 April 1973 at Jim Corbett National Park, under PM Indira Gandhi. Started with 9 reserves, now 55+. NTCA (National Tiger Conservation Authority) as statutory oversight — established 2005.

questions.stem: The ASIATIC LION is found ONLY in:
questions.explanation: Gir National Park, Junagadh district, Gujarat — only natural habitat of the Asiatic lion (Panthera leo persica) outside Africa. Population ~670 (2020 census). Smaller mane than African lion.
